title: Choose the visual world for Autonomous GitHub Resolver
question: This sets the colours, fonts and density for every screen. Keep the rolled direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Drafting Room Redline
options.lineage: engineering drawing revision control: whiteprints, redlines, revision clouds, the approval title block
options.thesis: Every agent change is a drawing revision: marked, numbered, traced to its source, and signed off by a human.
options.viewport: Prussian-blue side rail; whiteprint work area with the step tree left, live log right, and a title block (Drawn: agent / Checked / Approved: human) pinned to the run header.
options.risk: If the drafting cues grow past type, palette and the redline marks, it turns into a blueprint costume.

raised.raise: Every artifact gets a stable catalogue number (RUN-0142, CP-37, FLAG-3), quoted the same everywhere.
Redline red is reserved for the review trail (rollbacks, flags); ordinary errors use their own state colour.
One strict 4px cell module: every size is a whole multiple, and the step tree shows its grid as hairlines.
When the review gate opens, everything not under review dims; focus owns the screen.

options.label: Bound Lab Notebook
options.lineage: Good Laboratory Practice notebooks: numbered pages, single strike-through corrections, witness countersignature
options.thesis: The run is a signed lab record: nothing is erased, every correction is struck once and initialled, and a witness countersigns.
options.viewport: Black cover-board rail; pale ruled work area where rolled-back steps carry a single red strike with reason and checkpoint, and the review gate is a witness countersign block.
options.risk: Strong fit with the audit story, but it can drift toward paper nostalgia if the ruling or ink gets literal.

options.label: Monochrome Proof
options.thesis: A fine neutral scale and one accent; every claim the agent makes sits next to the evidence that proves it.
options.viewport: Light neutral shell, top bar plus side nav, run steps paired with their diff or log proof.
options.case: Developers recognise it instantly (holds audience identification), but it says nothing the category does not already say.
options.risk: Close to every dev tool on the market.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Runs are departures: ranked rows whose status restyles in place without the grid ever moving.
options.viewport: Dark shell; the org runs table as a live board where status changes flip character by character.
options.case: Strong product clarity for the live runs list (holds one axis); weaker on the review and diff screens.
options.risk: A dark board shell can read as a costume on form-heavy screens like settings.

options.label: Factory Catalogue
options.thesis: Every artifact is a numbered catalogue entry decoded by colour.
options.viewport: Black field, one plot, the run as a catalogue number.
options.case: Codes instead of labels hurt a working tool on both axes.
options.kept: Stable catalogue numbers for every run, step and flag.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Show only the next decision, in one reserved colour.
options.viewport: A yellow band naming the next decision.
options.case: Developers do not identify with it; clarity is no better than the roll's.
options.kept: One colour reserved for exactly one job.
options.risk: A yellow shell tires the eye over a workday.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid is visible and everything snaps to it.
options.viewport: Monumental grid letters over a visible armature.
options.case: A designer's world, not a developer's; display letterforms do not help the task.
options.kept: A strict cell module with a visible grid where it aids reading.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: The focused item grows; everything else steps back.
options.case: No artwork to carry it, and the wrong audience scene.
options.kept: Focus dimming when the review gate opens.
options.risk: An entertainment register on a security tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer dashboard every AI dev tool ships, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark side nav, run list and live terminal panes, blue primary buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
